findings: The process scan excluded ancestors and could miss an orphan native codec whose argv was only ./cmix.
Receipt branch selection and receipt hashing used separate path reads.
The planning sibling lock did not reserve the canonical full-1G namespace.
No durable activation intent, displaced predecessor, or recovery evidence survived a post-publication failure.
The verifiers did not independently bind the dispatch chain or its exact four-field derivation.

corrected_proofs.fact: One no-follow receipt descriptor supplies the parsed source value, branch boolean, SHA-256, verifier inputs, and final revalidation; the verifiers no longer reread the terminal receipt by pathname.

The shared scan considers every process except itself, with only a shell-launcher ancestry exception when command binding is the sole reason. Candidate/result/scratch/cgroup argv tokens, scratch cwd, cgroup membership, recorded PID/start identities, cgroup occupants, live lease ownership, and the canonical acquisition lock are all closed.

The activation receipt, intent, dispatch contract, selected plan, non-selected plan, schemas, runtime, helper, dispatcher, and source schema are rebound. Reverting revision, activation status, execution_authorized, and terminal_receipt_sha256 from the activated plan reproduces the exact frozen dormant bytes and SHA-256.
RENAME_EXCHANGE retains the exact displaced dormant inode at a deterministic recovery path, and the activation receipt binds that artifact instead of deleting it.

Each verifier prepares and fsyncs a complete schema-valid output under the full-1G lock, releases that lock, and only then publishes the canonical output with renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE). A lock-release failure therefore cannot leave an authoritative passing receipt.
The dispatcher imports neither subprocess nor signal, executes no verifier, creates no verifier receipt, and grants no Arm-B or parent-qualification authority.

remaining_non_authority_limits: A post-intent failure is fail-closed and retains reconstructive artifacts, but an inode-bound recovery transaction is not yet implemented.

The qm8 failure, dispatch-intent, and dispatch-activation schemas are direct-validated but are not yet registered in research_contracts.py; that live-bound module was intentionally not edited during qm8.

The terminal lease normally records the coordinator identity only. Native-codec closure is supplied by the all-process command, scratch-cwd, and cgroup scan unless a codec PID/start pair is actually present.
claim_boundary: This is static source and contract evidence, not a qm8 measurement or terminal result.
The live qm8 process, lease, cgroup, result tree, scratch tree, and candidate source were observed read-only and were not modified or signaled.
No q1 qualification, archive gain, inverse, runtime eligibility, Gamma compression credit, or Hutter score follows from this audit.
